Lines: Everyone is born to someone. Pick a people to go on.
What life did you lead before all this?
The most numerous folk of the valleys. Humans build, farm and trade, and fill Ashford's lanes. Short-lived, stubborn, and hard to discourage.
Long-lived and quiet, the elves remember things the villages have forgotten. A few still live among men, drawn by friendship or old debts.
Broad, green-skinned and slow to trust. Orcs came down from the northern highlands generations ago, and Ashford has learned to be glad of them.
Small, sharp-eared and sharper-eyed. Goblins notice what others walk past, and they're usually the first to hear a rumour.
You've walked more roads than most people in Ashford have heard of. You know how to read a trail and how to keep going when your feet say stop.
You grew up with the planting and the harvest. You know the fields, the woods behind them, and every face at the well.
You spent years copying old books for a scholar who never explained why. Some of what you read is starting to make sense.
You held a spear in someone else's war. You came home with a steady hand and a habit of watching the treeline.
For a long time nobody wanted you around, so you learned to need nobody. Then someone did want you around.
